title: Impact of Irrigation Eligibility on Crop Revenue

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method chosen: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD).  

Rationale: Eligibility for irrigation (treated = 1) is assigned mechanically once land‐slope (running_var) crosses a single threshold. Farmers cannot easily manipulate slope ex-ante, so observations just below and just above the cutoff are quasi-randomly assigned, mimicking a randomized experiment.  

Key assumptions  
1. Continuity: In the absence of treatment, the conditional expectation of crop revenue is smooth in land-slope at the cutoff.  
2. No precise manipulation: Farmers cannot sort exactly around the slope threshold, so the density of running_var is continuous at the cutoff.  

Given these, the jump in expected revenue at the cutoff identifies the causal effect of irrigation eligibility.

---

## 2. R Code
```r
#########################################################################
# Impact of irrigation eligibility on crop revenue – sharp RDD analysis #
#########################################################################

# 0. Packages ------------------------------------------------------------
need <- c("data.table","rdrobust")
new  <- need[!(need %in% installed.packages()[, "Package"])]
if(length(new)) install.packages(new, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
lapply(need, require, character.only = TRUE)

# 1. Read data -----------------------------------------------------------
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s96_data.csv"
df   <- fread(path)

# 2. Locate the cutoff programmatically ---------------------------------
# Sort by running variable
setorder(df, running_var)
# First occasion where treated switches from 0 to 1
switch_idx <- which(diff(df$treated) == 1)[1]
cutoff <- mean(df$running_var[c(switch_idx, switch_idx + 1)])
cat("Estimated cutoff (slope threshold) =", round(cutoff, 4), "\n\n")

# 3. Sharp RD using rdrobust --------------------------------------------
rd_main <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, p = 1, kernel = "triangular")

cat("Main estimate (local linear, IK bandwidth):\n")
print(summary(rd_main))

# Extract coefficient and p-value for concise reporting
tau  <- rd_main$coef[1]
pval <- rd_main$pv[1]
cat("\nEstimated jump in crop revenue =", round(tau, 4),
    "(p-value =", round(pval, 4), ")\n\n")

# 4. Basic robustness checks --------------------------------------------

## 4a. Quadratic specification
rd_quad <- rdrobust(df$y, df$running_var, c = cutoff, p = 2, kernel = "triangular")
cat("Quadratic polynomial estimate (p=2):", round(rd_quad$coef[1], 4),
    " p-value:", round(rd_quad$pv[1], 4), "\n")

## 4b. Half and double bandwidths
bw_IK <- rd_main$bws[1]          # Imbens–Kalyanaraman bandwidth on left
rd_half  <- rdrobust(df$y, df$running_var, c = cutoff,
                     h = bw_IK/2, kernel = "triangular")
rd_double <- rdrobust(df$y, df$running_var, c = cutoff,
                      h = bw_IK*2, kernel = "triangular")

cat("Half bandwidth estimate :", round(rd_half$coef[1], 4),
    " p-value:", round(rd_half$pv[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Double bandwidth estimate:", round(rd_double$coef[1], 4),
    " p-value:", round(rd_double$pv[1], 4), "\n")

# 5. Density test (manipulation check) ----------------------------------
# Minimal McCrary test (simple binomial test around cutoff)
library(grDevices)
bins  <- 30
hist_left  <- hist(df$running_var[df$running_var <  cutoff], plot = FALSE, breaks = bins)$counts
hist_right <- hist(df$running_var[df$running_var >= cutoff], plot = FALSE, breaks = bins)$counts
dens_test  <- t.test(hist_left, hist_right)
cat("\nManipulation check – t-test of bin heights left vs. right of cutoff:\n")
print(dens_test)
```

---

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Positive. Farmers who just qualify for irrigation should exhibit higher crop revenue because irrigation raises yields and stabilizes production.  

Magnitude: The outcome y appears standardized (mean ≈ 0, SD ≈ 0.3–0.4). A local jump of about 0.20–0.35 standard-deviation units (≈ 0.15–0.25 in these units) is plausible, translating to a roughly 15-25 % increase in revenue relative to farms just ineligible.  

Rationale: Prior agronomic studies find irrigation boosts output by 10-30 % in semi-arid regions; converting to standardized log-revenue units gives the above range.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare crop revenue for farms just above and below the slope threshold.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Eligibility for irrigation increases crop revenue.
